events.title: Generative AI Workshop: From Prompting to Prototyping
events.shortDescription: Hands-on intensive workshop transitioning students from fundamental prompt engineering to building end-to-end autonomous agent workflows.
events.description: An intensive technical immersion into enterprise-grade Generative AI engineering. Designed for Computer Science undergraduates, this program bridges transformer theory with production RAG implementations using pgvector and LangGraph orchestrations, fostering hands-on mastery over autonomous agentic workflows.
objectives: Demystify LLM tokenization, temperature, system conditioning, and vector embeddings through practical code sandboxes.
Equip students to connect vector databases (pgvector/ChromaDB) with local embedding pipelines for verifiable semantic search.
Deliver working knowledge of ethical AI parameters, academic integrity safeguards, and hallucination reduction strategies.
events.locationDetails: Turing Hall, Gate 1 & 2 Main Tier-1 Lab Complex
events.targetAudience: 2nd & 3rd Year B.Tech CSE / IT / Data Science Undergraduates
events.eligibility: Basic proficiency in Python 3.10+ and foundational data structures.
events.participationInstructions: Bring personal laptop with Python 3.10+ installed and Git configured. Cloud sandbox tokens and API credentials will be provisioned directly at gate check-in.

speaker.name: Faculty Coordinator (AI Lab)
speaker.designation: Director, Campus AI & Autonomous Systems Research Lab
speaker.organization: Ex-Google Research Fellow • Carnegie Mellon Alum
speaker.bio: Dr. Jenkins holds a doctorate in Distributed Cognitive Systems from Carnegie Mellon. Her lab focuses on low-latency inference on edge silicon and provable alignment bounds for agent architectures.

agenda.sessionTitle: Keynote: Theoretical Foundations of Transformer Architectures
agenda.description: Attention layers, query-key vectors, self-attention matrices, and quantization benchmarks.

agenda.sessionTitle: Hands-on Sandbox: Prompt Chaining & Multi-agent Orchestration
agenda.description: Building modular pipelines using LangGraph and function-calling schemas in cloud notebooks.

agenda.sessionTitle: Building Production RAG with Vector Embeddings
agenda.description: Chunking university documentation, cosine indexing via pgvector, and hybrid keyword-vector reranking.

agenda.sessionTitle: Project Submission, Q&A, and Verified Digital Credential Issuance
agenda.description: Code artifact commit to GitHub Classroom, rapid gate scan checkout, and micro-credential verification.

requirements.prerequisites: Foundations of Computer Science, Python OOP basics, familiarity with terminal/CLI.
requirements.thingsToBring: Laptop with charger, campus ID card, wired headphones.
requirements.softwareTools: Python 3.10+, VS Code or Cursor IDE, Git, browser with Chrome/Firefox.
requirements.otherInstructions: Complimentary high-speed campus sandbox Wi-Fi will be authenticated through Student Pass ID.

events.syllabusMapping: CSE-8402: Advanced Artificial Intelligence (Module 4 & 5 Outcome Aligned)
events.hodReviewComment: Approved. Certified curriculum tie-in for CSE department.

events.title: Cloud Native Microservices Bootcamp
events.shortDescription: Deep dive into containerization, Kubernetes clusters, service meshes, and distributed tracing.
events.description: Learn how to architect, containerize, and deploy resilient microservices systems using Docker, Kubernetes, and gRPC in real university cloud clusters.
objectives: Understand container namespaces and cgroups.
Deploy multi-tier container topologies with ingress controllers.
Monitor distributed transactions with OpenTelemetry.
events.participationInstructions: SSH keys will be validated on local workstations.

speaker.name: Cloud Lab Coordinator (CSE)
speaker.bio: 15 years architecting large-scale telecom distributed backends.

agenda.description: Building multi-stage scratch containers with minimal attack surfaces.
Hands-on deployment to live k3s department sandbox.

requirements.thingsToBring: Personal laptop with SSH client installed.

events.hodReviewComment: Approved. Essential curriculum tie-in for Cloud Computing lab requirements.

events.title: ACM 24-Hour Hackathon: Campus Hack 2026
events.shortDescription: The annual flagship 24-hour university hackathon addressing real-world sustainability, fintech, and AI challenges.
events.description: Campus Hack brings together 350+ student developers, designers, and domain innovators for 24 hours of non-stop rapid prototyping, supported by industry mentors and $5,000 in grand prize awards.
objectives: Build fully functional MVP solving sustainability or education challenges.
Collaborate across interdisciplinary student teams under strict deadline pressure.
Present live architectural demonstrations to university and industry judges.
events.targetAudience: All University Students across Engineering, Sciences & Design
events.eligibility: Open to enrolled students in teams of 2 to 4 members.
events.participationInstructions: Check-in begins at 08:30 AM at Central Atrium Gate A. Bring valid university ID and sleeping gear if staying overnight.

speaker.name: Cybersecurity Mentors
speaker.bio: Leading student technical competitive chapters and mentor networks.

agenda.description: Track disclosures: Clean Energy, AI for Good, Financial Inclusion.
Code sanity checks and deployment testing.
Live 3-minute stage demonstrations in front of the jury.

requirements.prerequisites: Git repository initialized on GitHub / GitLab, valid student status.
requirements.thingsToBring: Hardware accessories, personal laptops, extension cords.

events.syllabusMapping: NAAC Metric 3.3.2 Co-Curricular Innovation & Project Incubation
events.hodReviewComment: Approved department flagship. Budget and 24-hr facility access cleared with campus security.

events.title: Industry Expert Talk: Scaling Distributed Databases
events.shortDescription: CockroachDB VP on consensus algorithms, Raft replication, multi-region transactions, and geo-partitioning.
events.description: An exclusive technical session with veteran database architects from CockroachDB exploring the engineering realities of globally distributed SQL databases, Raft consensus consensus, and ACID guarantees.
objectives: Grasp Raft consensus state machines and log replication.
Analyze two-phase commit overhead in WAN environments.
Explore geo-partitioning architectures for sub-10ms transactional reads.
events.participationInstructions: Seating on first-come-first-admitted basis for confirmed pass holders.

speaker.name: Marcus Chen
speaker.bio: Leading database researcher specializing in Paxos/Raft consensus and hybrid logical clocks.

agenda.description: Overcoming clock drift in distributed commit protocols.
Simulating region partition failures and automatic leader re-election.

requirements.prerequisites: Relational database concepts (ACID, transaction isolation levels).

events.syllabusMapping: CSE-5401: Database Management Systems & Advanced Storage
events.hodReviewComment: Approved with distinguished industrial sync certification.

events.title: Competitive Programming League: Division 1
events.shortDescription: Speed algorithmic challenges focusing on advanced dynamic programming and graph theory.
events.description: Bi-weekly algorithmic arena hosted on the campus judging server. Test problem-solving under extreme time constraints with automated test-suite evaluations.
objectives: Master segment trees, Fenwick trees, and lowest common ancestor queries.
Optimize algorithm runtime to meet strict 1.0s and 256MB memory limits.
events.eligibility: Proficiency in C++, Java, or Python.
events.participationInstructions: Bring personal laptop or use lab workstations.

speaker.name: Algorithms Coordinator (CSE)
speaker.bio: Author of 3 algorithmic textbooks and coach of national championship squads.

requirements.prerequisites: Data Structures and Algorithms course completion.

events.hodReviewComment: Approved. Excellent preparation for ICPC regionals.

events.title: Advanced Deep Learning & Transformer Quantization Seminar
events.shortDescription: Research seminar on 4-bit and 8-bit post-training quantization and speculative decoding for edge GPUs.
events.description: Detailed analysis of GPTQ, AWQ, and speculative decoding techniques to compress multi-billion parameter models into constrained edge devices.
objectives: Compare weight-only vs activation quantization trade-offs.
Benchmark perplexity loss across llama-3.1-8b variants.

speaker.name: Faculty Coordinator (CSE)
speaker.bio: Expert in embedded neural network compression.

events.hodReviewComment: Please recheck the lab compute budget requirements for GPU instances. Provide allocation code under IEEE grant pool before statutory sign-off.

events.title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) Intensive
events.shortDescription: Step-by-step training of reward models and proximal policy optimization (PPO) for conversational alignment.
events.description: Draft proposal exploring reward modeling, Bradley-Terry preference scoring, and PPO loss formulation.
objectives: Implement pairwise ranking loss in PyTorch.
Run PPO fine-tuning loop with KL divergence penalty.

speaker.name: Faculty Coordinator (CSE)
speaker.bio: Research lead in alignment and safety.

agenda.description: Dataset annotation schema and loss computation.

requirements.softwareTools: CUDA capable GPU or Google Colab.

Deploy ONNX models onto TensorRT acceleration engines.
